prompt:
Produce two blocks about the image, in exactly this format:

<TAGS>
tag_one, tag_two, tag_three
</TAGS>
<CAPTION>
one paragraph of description
</CAPTION>

<TAGS> rules:
- 12 to 160 tags, lowercase, words joined by underscores (danbooru style: long_hair, looking_at_viewer, depth_of_field).
- Order from most to least salient; separate with commas only.
- Most images land around 30-60 tags; go higher only when the image really is that dense.
- Never pad the list to reach 12: near-duplicates and restatements of the same fact waste slots. On a simple image, spend the slots on framing, lighting and background instead.
- Only tag what is clearly visible: subject count and type, hair, eyes, clothing, pose, action, setting, props, camera angle, framing, lighting, colour palette, art style.
- Do not tag the image's text: no words, signs, labels, prices, dates or bubble lines. One `text` tag covers a text-heavy image.
- Do not output quality or score words (masterpiece, best quality, 8k, highres, ultra detailed).
- Do not output the artist name, the character name, or the series name: you cannot know them and guessing poisons the label.

<CAPTION> rules:
- One paragraph of 400-1024 characters (roughly 4-9 sentences), on a single line. This character range is a guide, not a cutoff; finish complete sentences and keep essential visible details within the training-token budget.
- Order the content: main subject; setting and background; composition and camera angle when clear; lighting; only short, prominent, clearly legible text when useful, quoted verbatim inside double quotes.
- Mention colour and surface/material details for the main subject and other prominent objects when they are clearly visible and useful. Omit uncertain details; do not infer material from colour, lighting or context.
- Describe clearly visible spatial relationships between main subjects (position, overlap or contact) when they help explain the scene. Omit them when they are unclear or irrelevant.
- Describe only what is visible. Do not speculate about anything outside the frame.
- Do not name or guess the artist, character, series or studio. A signature or watermark is visible text, not proof of authorship; quote it only if prominent and useful, and never resolve it into a name. Trusted artist metadata is added separately by the annotation system.
- When clearly distinguishable, name the overall art style and medium in one clause (anime illustration, watercolour, oil painting, 3D render, photograph); mention line work and finish only when clearly visible.
- English only, plain prose: no markdown, no bullet points, no headings, no "Caption:" prefix.
- Quote only short, clearly legible text that is prominent and useful for understanding the image, verbatim in its original script.
- never translate the text, and never romanise non-Latin scripts.
- Keep original punctuation and reading order within a quotation. Omit illegible text; never guess missing characters or add [unreadable] placeholders.
- For dense dialogue, many speech bubbles, repeated labels or tiny background print, mention their presence in one brief clause if visually important; do not transcribe or retell their contents, count every bubble or list each text region. If text itself is the main subject, quote at most one short, prominent, clearly legible phrase.
- Do not describe the font or layout unless the text itself is the subject.
- A quoted date, year or timestamp is visible text only; never use it to infer when the work was made or which era its style belongs to.
- When the image has no text, leave text out of the caption entirely.
- Aim for at most 384 tokens of description. This is a soft target: essential detail may exceed it, but the final training text must not exceed 512 tokens. Prioritize the subject and setting; shorten repeated details and small print. Do not pad to reach the target.

Output these two blocks, in this order, and nothing else.
prompt_zh:
Produce two blocks about the image, in exactly this format:

<TAGS>
tag_one, tag_two, tag_three
</TAGS>
<CAPTION>
one paragraph of description
</CAPTION>

<TAGS> rules:
- 12 to 160 tags, lowercase, words joined by underscores (danbooru style: long_hair, looking_at_viewer, depth_of_field).
- Order from most to least salient; separate with commas only.
- Most images land around 30-60 tags; go higher only when the image really is that dense.
- Never pad the list to reach 12: near-duplicates and restatements of the same fact waste slots. On a simple image, spend the slots on framing, lighting and background instead.
- Only tag what is clearly visible: subject count and type, hair, eyes, clothing, pose, action, setting, props, camera angle, framing, lighting, colour palette, art style.
- Do not tag the image's text: no words, signs, labels, prices, dates or bubble lines. One `text` tag covers a text-heavy image.
- Do not output quality or score words (masterpiece, best quality, 8k, highres, ultra detailed).
- Do not output the artist name, the character name, or the series name: you cannot know them and guessing poisons the label.

<CAPTION> 规则：
- 一段连续的中文散文，约 69-176 个汉字，单行、不换行。字数区间是引导，不是截断线；句子写完整，在训练 token 预算内保留必要的可见细节。
- 内容顺序：主体；场景与背景；构图，以及清楚可辨时的机位；光线；仅在有助于理解画面时，用双引号原样引用简短、显著且清楚可辨的文字。
- 主要主体之间有助于理解画面的相对位置、遮挡或接触关系时，简要说明；没有明显关系或看不清时无需补写。
- 只在机位或透视清楚且有助于理解画面时说明；画面简单或角度不明确时可以省略。
- 颜色和表面质感只写主要主体及显著物件中清晰可见且有用的特征；不确定时省略，不要根据颜色、光影或上下文推断材质。
- 只写画面里看得见的东西，不要推测画框外的内容。
- 不要点名或猜测画师、角色、系列、工作室。签名或水印属于可见文字，不能证明画师身份；只有显著且有用时才引用，不把它解释成人名。可信画师信息由标注系统另行注入。
- 用一句话说明清楚可辨的整体画风与媒介（日式插画、水彩、油画、3D 渲染、摄影）；线条与完成度只在画面能明确看出时描述。
- 这一段必须用简体中文写，不要用英文。纯散文：不要 markdown、不要分条、不要小标题、不要"描述："这类前缀。
- 只引用简短、清楚可辨、显著且有助于理解画面的文字，保持原字形与原标点。
- 不要翻译，也不要把非拉丁文字转写成拼音或罗马字。
- 引文保留原标点与阅读顺序。看不清的文字直接省略，不猜缺字，不添加 [无法辨认] 占位符。
- 密集对白、多处对话气泡、重复标签或背景小字，只有影响画面构成时才用一个短句概括其存在；不抄写或复述内容，不逐个数气泡，也不逐块罗列。文字本身就是主体时，最多引用一处简短、显著且清楚可辨的文字。
- 除非文字本身就是画面主体，否则不描述字体与排版。
- 引用的日期、年份或时间戳只作为可见文字，不用于推断作品创作年代或画风年代。
- 整张图没有任何文字时，整段不要提文字。
- 描述尽量控制在 384 token 以内；必要细节可以超过这个软目标，但最终训练文本不得超过 512 token。优先保留主体与场景，精简重复细节和小字，不为达到长度目标补写内容。

Output these two blocks, in this order, and nothing else.
system: You annotate images for diffusion-model training data. You are precise and literal: you describe only what is visible in the image. You never guess the artist, the character, or the series.
note: 内置提示词的快照（按默认产出规格生成）；改这里不影响「内置（按参数生成）」那一项
